   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>Note <em style="font: inherit;">1.</em> Basis of Presentation</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:25pt;">HeartSciences Inc. (&#8220;HeartSciences&#8221; or the &#8220;Company&#8221;) is a healthcare information technology company focused on advancing electrocardiography (&#8220;ECG&#8221; or &#8220;EKG&#8221;) through the integration of artificial intelligence (&#8220;AI&#8221;). The Company has developed MyoVista Insights&#8482;, a cloud-native, vendor- and device-agnostic ECG management platform designed to improve workflow efficiency, streamline data management, and support the deployment of <em style="font: inherit;">third</em>-party AI-ECG algorithms. MyoVista Insights is classified as a Medical Device Data System (&#8220;MDDS&#8221;) and is exempt from U.S. Food and Drug Administration (&#8220;FDA&#8221;) <em style="font: inherit;">510</em>(k) requirements. HeartSciences has also developed the MyoVista&#174; <i>wav</i>ECG&#8482; device, which provides conventional ECG functionality and is designed to host AI-ECG algorithms. The Company submitted the MyoVista <i>wav</i>ECG device to the FDA for <em style="font: inherit;">510</em>(k) premarket clearance in <em style="font: inherit;"> December 2025 </em>and has licensed or developed additional AI-ECG algorithms that <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>be submitted for regulatory clearance in the future.&#160;The Company is a Texas corporation and is headquartered in Southlake, Texas.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:25pt;">On <em style="font: inherit;"> May 6, 2024, </em>the Company filed a Certificate of Amendment to the Amended and Restated Certificate of Formation with the Secretary of the State of the state of Texas to effect a <em style="font: inherit;">1</em>-for-<ix:nonFraction id="c142002076" contextRef="d_2024-05-06_2024-05-06_NonmonetaryTransactionTypeAxis-ReverseStockSplitMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:StockholdersEquityNoteStockSplitConversionRatio1" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">100</ix:nonFraction> reverse stock split (the &#8220;Reverse Stock Split&#8221;) of its outstanding shares of common stock, $<ix:nonFraction id="c142002077" contextRef="i_2026-01-31" unitRef="USDPerShare" name="us-gaap:CommonStockParOrStatedValuePerShare" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">0.001</ix:nonFraction> par value per share (the &#8220;Common Stock&#8221;), with an effective date of <em style="font: inherit;"> May 17, 2024. </em>As a result of the Reverse Stock Split, every <ix:nonFraction id="c142002078" contextRef="d_2024-05-06_2024-05-06_NonmonetaryTransactionTypeAxis-ReverseStockSplitMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:StockholdersEquityNoteStockSplitConversionRatio1" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">100</ix:nonFraction> shares of the Company's issued and outstanding pre-reverse split Common Stock were combined into <em style="font: inherit;">one</em> share of Common Stock, except to the extent that the Reverse Stock Split resulted in any of the Company's shareholders owning a fractional share, which was rounded up to the next highest whole share. In connection with the Reverse Stock Split, there was <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> change in the par value per share of $<ix:nonFraction id="c142002081" contextRef="i_2024-05-06" unitRef="USDPerShare" name="us-gaap:CommonStockParOrStatedValuePerShare" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">0.001</ix:nonFraction>. As a result of the Reverse Stock Split, equitable adjustments corresponding to the Reverse Stock Split ratio will be made to the Company&#8217;s outstanding warrants and upon the exercise or vesting of all stock options such that every <em style="font: inherit;">one hundred</em> (<ix:nonFraction id="c142002083" contextRef="d_2024-05-06_2024-05-06_NonmonetaryTransactionTypeAxis-ReverseStockSplitMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:StockholdersEquityNoteStockSplitConversionRatio1" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">100</ix:nonFraction>) shares of Common Stock that <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>be issued upon the exercise of the warrants and stock options held immediately prior to the Reverse Stock Split will represent <em style="font: inherit;">one</em> share of Common Stock that <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>be issued upon exercise of such warrants and stock options immediately following the Reverse Stock Split. Correspondingly, the exercise price per share of Common Stock attributable to the warrants and stock options immediately prior to the Reverse Stock Split will be proportionately increased by a multiple of <ix:nonFraction id="c142002085" contextRef="d_2024-05-06_2024-05-06_NonmonetaryTransactionTypeAxis-ReverseStockSplitMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:StockholdersEquityNoteStockSplitConversionRatio1" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">100</ix:nonFraction> following the Reverse Stock Split.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:25pt;">All Common Stock share and per share data, and exercise price data for applicable Common Stock equivalents, included in these financial statements have been retroactively adjusted to give effect to the Reverse Stock Split for all periods presented, unless otherwise indicated.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>Note <em style="font: inherit;">2.</em> Liquidity, Going Concern and Other Uncertainties</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:25pt;">The Company is subject to a number of risks similar to those of early-stage companies, including dependence on key individuals and products, the difficulties inherent in the development of a commercial market, the need to obtain additional capital, competition from larger companies, and other technologies.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:25pt;">The Company has incurred losses each year since inception and has experienced negative cash flows from operations in each year since inception. At&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> January 31, 2026</em> and <em style="font: inherit;"> April 30, 2025</em>, the Company had an accumulated deficit of&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c142002087" contextRef="i_2026-01-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:RetainedEarningsAccumulatedDeficit" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5" sign="-">82.5</ix:nonFraction> million&#160;and $<ix:nonFraction id="c142002088" contextRef="i_2025-04-30" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:RetainedEarningsAccumulatedDeficit" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5" sign="-">76.1</ix:nonFraction> million, respectively. These factors raise substantial doubt regarding the Company's ability to continue as a going concern.</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>Note <em style="font: inherit;">3.</em> Summary of Significant Accounting Policies</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b></b></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-05-01_2026-01-31" name="us-gaap:BasisOfAccountingPolicyPolicyTextBlock" id="c142005092" escape="true"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>Basis of Presentation</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:25pt;">The accompanying unaudited condensed financial statements have been prepared in conformity with accounting principles generally accepted in the United States of America (&#8220;US GAAP&#8221;) and in conformity with the instructions on Form <em style="font: inherit;">10</em>-Q and Rule <em style="font: inherit;">8</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">03</em> of Regulation S-<em style="font: inherit;">X</em> and the related rules and regulations of the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commissions (&#8220;SEC&#8221;) and have been prepared on a basis which assumes that the Company will continue as a going concern, which contemplates the realization of assets and the satisfaction of liabilities and commitments in the normal course of business. In the opinion of management, the unaudited interim financial statements reflect all adjustments, which include only normal recurring adjustments necessary for the fair statement of the balances and results of operations for the periods presented. The interim operating results are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> necessarily indicative of results that <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>be expected for any subsequent period. The accompanying unaudited condensed financial statements should be read in conjunction with the Company's audited financial statements and notes thereto included in the <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em> Annual Report on Form <em style="font: inherit;">10</em>-K.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"></p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b></b></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-05-01_2026-01-31" name="us-gaap:UseOfEstimates" id="c142005093" escape="true"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>Use of Estimates</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:25pt;">The preparation of financial statements in conformity with US GAAP requires management to make estimates and assumptions that affect the reported amounts of assets and liabilities, and the disclosure of contingent assets and liabilities as of the date of the financial statements, and the reported amounts of revenues and expenses during the reporting periods. Actual results could differ from those estimates.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"></p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b></b></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-05-01_2026-01-31" name="us-gaap:CashAndCashEquivalentsPolicyTextBlock" id="c142005094" escape="true"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>Cash and Cash Equivalents</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:25pt;">The Company considers all highly liquid investments with original maturities of <em style="font: inherit;">three</em> months or less to be cash equivalents. The fair value of cash and cash equivalents approximates carrying value. At times, the Company&#8217;s cash balances <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>exceed the current insured amounts under the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (&#8220;FDIC&#8221;).</p>

   </ix:nonNumeric>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:25pt;">Inventory consists mainly of raw materials and components used in the current hardware build of the MyoVista <i>wav</i>ECG devices and components are used for research and development purposes and device sales, which to date have been in international markets as sale of the MyoVista <i>wav</i>ECG in the U.S. is subject to FDA clearance. Management believes that its hardware platform is in final form, however, prior to FDA clearance and market acceptance of the MyoVista <i>wav</i>ECG, further hardware changes could be necessary which could have an impact on net realizable values. The majority of the Company&#8217;s current inventory is intended for use to build finished products following regulatory clearance. Finished products do <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> contain materials that would degrade significantly over the useable life of the device and are considered to have a useable life of over <em style="font: inherit;">seven</em> years. Existing inventory related to finished devices are planned to be updated to the latest hardware revision and specifically allocated to a limited distribution for field reliability studies and are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> slated for general purpose sales. The Company periodically evaluates inventory and makes specific write-offs and provides an allowance for inventory that is considered obsolete due to hardware and or software related changes. If the Company does <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> receive FDA clearance and/or obtain market acceptance of the MyoVista <i>wav</i>ECG, the Company could have further material write-downs of inventory due to obsolescence in excess of the amount currently reserved.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p></ix:nonNumeric><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-05-01_2026-01-31" name="us-gaap:ResearchAndDevelopmentExpensePolicy" id="c142005096" escape="true"><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"></p><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>Research and Development Expenses</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:25pt;">In accordance with ASC Topic <em style="font: inherit;">730,</em> <i>Accounting for Research and Development Costs, </i>the Company accounts for research and development expenditures, including payments to collaborative research partners and regulatory filing costs, as research and development expenses.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 25pt; text-align: justify;">The Company also applies the principles of ASC <em style="font: inherit;">985</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">20,</em> <i>Accounting for the Costs of Computer Software to Be Sold, Leased, or Otherwise Marketed</i> (&#8220;ASC <em style="font: inherit;">985</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">20&#8221;</em>). ASC <em style="font: inherit;">985</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">20</em> requires that software development costs incurred in conjunction with product development be charged to research and development expense until technological feasibility is established.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"></p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b></b></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-05-01_2026-01-31" name="us-gaap:ResearchDevelopmentAndComputerSoftwarePolicyTextBlock" id="c142005097" escape="true"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>Software Development Costs</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:25pt;">The costs incurred for the development of computer software to be sold, leased, or otherwise marketed are capitalized in accordance with ASC <em style="font: inherit;">985</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">20,</em> when technological feasibility has been established. Technological feasibility generally occurs when all planning, design, coding, and testing activities are completed that are necessary to establish that the product can be produced to meet its design specifications, including functions, features, and technical performance requirements.&#160;Based on our software development process, technological feasibility is established upon the completion of a working model that contains essentially all the functionality and features of a final model. The completeness and consistency of the working model have been confirmed through testing.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:25pt;">Costs incurred during the period of planning and design, prior to the period of determining technological feasibility, has been charged to operations in the period incurred as research and development costs. Capitalization of software development costs begins upon the establishment of technological feasibility and reported at the lower of unamortized cost or net realizable value. Capitalization is discontinued when the product is made available for sale.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:25pt;">Amortization of capitalized development costs for externally marketed software commences when the product is available for commercial release. Capitalized software development costs are amortized using the greater of (a) the amount computed using the ratio that current gross revenue for a product bear to total of current and anticipated future gross revenue for that product or (b) the straight-line method, beginning upon commercial release of the product, and continuing over the remaining estimated economic life of the product.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 25pt;">As of <em style="font: inherit;"> January 31, 2026</em>, capitalized product development costs related to MyoVista Insights were $<ix:nonFraction id="c142002200" contextRef="i_2026-01-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:CapitalizedComputerSoftwareNet" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">457,123</ix:nonFraction>. <em style="font: inherit;">No</em> amortization was recorded during the&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">nine</em>&#160;months&#160;ended&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> January 31, 2026</em>, as the software was <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> yet available for commercial release.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"></p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><b></b></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-05-01_2026-01-31" name="us-gaap:PropertyPlantAndEquipmentPolicyTextBlock" id="c142005098" escape="true"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><b>Property and Equipment</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:25pt;">Property and equipment are recorded at cost less accumulated depreciation. Depreciation is computed using the straight-line method over the estimated useful lives. The range of estimated useful lives used to calculate depreciation is generally <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="i_2026-01-31_RangeAxis-MinimumMember" name="us-gaap:PropertyPlantAndEquipmentUsefulLife" id="c142002205" format="ixt-sec:duryear">3</ix:nonNumeric> to <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="i_2026-01-31_RangeAxis-MaximumMember" name="us-gaap:PropertyPlantAndEquipmentUsefulLife" id="c142002206" format="ixt-sec:duryear">5</ix:nonNumeric> years. Ordinary maintenance and repairs are charged to expense as incurred, and replacements and betterments are capitalized. When items are retired or otherwise disposed, the related cost and accumulated depreciation are removed from the accounts and any resulting gain or loss is reflected in other income (expense).</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"></p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b></b></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-05-01_2026-01-31" name="us-gaap:DeferredChargesPolicyTextBlock" id="c142005099" escape="true"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>Deferred Offering Costs</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:25pt;">The Company capitalizes certain legal, professional, and other-<em style="font: inherit;">third</em> party charges related to its efforts to raise capital and other ongoing equity financings as deferred offering costs until fully consummated. These costs are deferred until the completion of the offerings at which time they are reclassified to additional paid-in-capital as a reduction of the offering proceeds. If the Company terminates the planned offering, all of the deferred offering costs will be immediately written off to operating expenses.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:25pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:25pt;">In <em style="font: inherit;"> March 2023, </em>the Company entered into a purchase agreement and registration rights agreement with an institutional investor, providing for the sale, from time to time at the discretion of the Company, of up to $<ix:nonFraction id="c142002208" contextRef="i_2023-03-31_SubsidiarySaleOfStockAxis-LincolnParkAgreementMember" unitRef="USD" name="hscs:SaleOfStockValueAuthorized" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-6">15.0</ix:nonFraction> million of the Company's Common Stock, over the <em style="font: inherit;">thirty-six</em> (<em style="font: inherit;">36</em>) month term of the purchase agreement. Deferred offering costs associated with the Equity Line are reclassified to additional paid in capital on a pro-rata basis over the term of the agreement.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:25pt;">In <em style="font: inherit;"> September 2023, </em>the Company entered into an EDA to sell its Common Stock under the ATM Facility. Deferred offering costs associated with the ATM Facility are reclassified to additional paid in capital on a pro-rata basis.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:25pt;">In <em style="font: inherit;"> March 2025, </em>the Company filed an offering statement on Form <em style="font: inherit;">1</em>-A with the SEC for the sale of preferred stock and warrants. Deferred offering costs associated with this offering are reclassified to additional paid in capital on a pro-rata basis.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:25pt;">As of <em style="font: inherit;"> January 31, 2026</em> and <em style="font: inherit;"> April 30, 2025</em>, $<ix:nonFraction id="c142002212" contextRef="i_2026-01-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DeferredOfferingCosts" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">822,206</ix:nonFraction>&#160;and&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c142002213" contextRef="i_2025-04-30" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DeferredOfferingCosts" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">290,925</ix:nonFraction>&#160;of deferred offering costs were capitalized on the balance sheet, respectively.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"></p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b></b></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-05-01_2026-01-31" name="us-gaap:FairValueMeasurementPolicyPolicyTextBlock" id="c142005100" escape="true"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>Fair Value Measurements</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:25pt;">The accounting guidance establishes a consistent framework for measuring fair value and expands disclosure for each major asset and liability category measured at fair value on either a recurring or nonrecurring basis. Fair value is defined as the exchange price that would be received for an asset or paid to transfer a liability in the principal or most advantageous market for the asset transaction between market participants on the measurement date. Where available, fair value is based on observable market prices or is derived from such prices. As such, fair value is a market-based measurement that should be determined based on assumptions that market participants would use in pricing an asset or liability.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:25pt;">As a basis for considering such assumptions, the accounting guidance establishes a <em style="font: inherit;">three</em>-tier fair value hierarchy, which prioritizes the inputs used in measuring fair value as follows:</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;"><tbody><tr><td style="width:25pt;">&#160;</td><td style="vertical-align:top;width:18pt;"> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#9679;</p> </td><td style="vertical-align:top;"> <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Level <em style="font: inherit;">1</em> &#8211;&#160;Observable inputs such as quoted prices in active markets;</p> </td></tr>
</tbody></table>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;"><tbody><tr><td style="width:25pt;">&#160;</td><td style="vertical-align:top;width:18pt;"> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#9679;</p> </td><td style="vertical-align:top;"> <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Level <em style="font: inherit;">2</em> &#8211;&#160;Inputs, other than the quoted prices in active markets, that are observable either directly or indirectly;</p> </td></tr>
</tbody></table>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;"><tbody><tr><td style="width:25pt;">&#160;</td><td style="vertical-align:top;width:18pt;"> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#9679;</p> </td><td style="vertical-align:top;"> <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Level <em style="font: inherit;">3</em> &#8211;&#160;Unobservable inputs in which there is little or <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> market data, which require the reporting entity to develop its own assumptions.</p> </td></tr>
</tbody></table>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:25pt;">In certain cases, the inputs used to measure fair value <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>fall into different levels of the fair value hierarchy. In such cases, the assignment of an asset or liability within the fair value hierarchy is based on the lowest level of input that is significant to the fair value measurement.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:25pt;">Management&#8217;s assessment of the significance of a particular input to the fair value measurement in its entirety requires judgment and considers factors specific to the asset or liability. The carrying amounts of the Company&#8217;s financial instruments, which primarily include cash and cash equivalents, accounts payable and accrued expenses, approximate their fair values due to their short-term nature. The carrying amounts of the Company&#8217;s existing notes payable approximate their fair values at the stated interest rates and are reflective of the prevailing market rates.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>

       <em style="font: inherit;">9</em>

   <ix:exclude>&#160;</ix:exclude>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"></p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b></b></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-05-01_2026-01-31" name="us-gaap:ImpairmentOrDisposalOfLongLivedAssetsIncludingIntangibleAssetsPolicyPolicyTextBlock" id="c142005101" escape="true"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>Long-Lived Assets</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:25pt;">Long-lived assets, such as equipment, software development costs, and intangible assets, are reviewed for impairment whenever events or changes in circumstances indicate that the carrying amount of an asset <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em><em style="font: inherit;">not</em> be recoverable. If circumstances require a long-lived asset or asset group be tested for possible impairment, the Company <em style="font: inherit;">first</em> compares undiscounted cash flows expected to be generated by that asset or asset group to its carrying amount. If the carrying amount of the long-lived asset or asset group is determined to <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> be recoverable on an undiscounted cash flow basis, an impairment is recognized to the extent the carrying amount exceeds its fair value.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"></p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><b></b></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-05-01_2026-01-31" name="us-gaap:LesseeLeasesPolicyTextBlock" id="c142005102" escape="true"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><b>Leases</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:25pt;">The Company determines if a contract is or contains a lease at inception or modification of a contract. A contract is or contains a lease if the contract conveys the right to control the use of an identified asset for a period in exchange for consideration. Control over the use of the identified asset means the lessee has both (a) the right to obtain substantially all of the economic benefits from the use of the asset and (b) the right to direct the use of the asset. Right-of-use assets and liabilities are recognized based on the present value of future minimum lease payments over the expected lease term at commencement date. The Company measures and records a right-of-use asset and lease liability based on the discount rate implicit in the lease, if known. In cases where the discount rate implicit in the lease is <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> known, the Company measures the right-of-use assets and lease liabilities using a discount rate equal to the Company&#8217;s estimated incremental borrowing rate for loans with similar collateral and duration.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:25pt;">The Company elected to <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> apply the recognition requirements to leases of all classes of underlying assets that, at the commencement date, have a lease term of <em style="font: inherit;">12</em> months or less and do <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> include an option to purchase the underlying asset that the lessee is reasonably certain to exercise. Instead, lease payments for such short-term leases are recognized in operations on a straight-line basis over the lease term and variable lease payments in the period in which the obligation for those payments is incurred.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"></p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b></b></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-05-01_2026-01-31" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationOptionAndIncentivePlansPolicy" id="c142005103" escape="true"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>Stock-Based Compensation</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:25pt;">The Company accounts for employee and non-employee share-based compensation in accordance with the provisions of ASC <em style="font: inherit;">718,</em> <i>Compensation </i>&#8211;<i> Stock Compensation</i>. Under ASC <em style="font: inherit;">718,</em> share-based compensation cost is measured at the grant date, based on the calculated fair value of the award, and is recognized as an expense over the requisite service period (generally the vesting period of the equity grant).</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:25pt;">The Company grants stock options, restricted stock units (&#8220;RSUs&#8221;), and restricted stock awards (&#8220;RSAs&#8221;)&#160;under its <em style="font: inherit;">2023</em> Equity Incentive Plan, as amended. The Company measures all share-based payment awards at their grant-date fair value. The fair value of each option is estimated on the date of grant using the Black-Scholes option-pricing model that uses assumptions for expected volatility, expected dividends, expected forfeiture rate, expected term, and the risk-free interest rate. These assumptions are primarily based on historical data, peer company data and the judgment of management regarding future trends and other factors.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:25pt;">Management has estimated the expected term of its Common Stock options using the &#8220;simplified&#8221; method, whereby, the expected term equals the arithmetic average of the vesting term and the original contractual term of the option due to its lack of sufficient historical data. The risk-free interest rates for periods within the expected term of the option are based on the US Treasury securities with a maturity date that commensurate with the expected term of the associated award. There is <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> expected dividend yield since the Company has never paid cash dividends and does <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> expect to pay cash dividends in the foreseeable future.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:25pt;">For stock options issued to employees and non-employees, the fair value of stock-based awards is recognized as compensation expense over the requisite service period, which is defined as the period during which an employee is required to provide service in exchange for an award. The Company uses a straight-line attribution method for all grants that include only a service condition. The Company accounts for forfeitures when they occur. Stock-based compensation expense recognized in the financial statements is reduced by actual awards forfeited. For RSUs issued to employees, the Company recognizes the grant date fair value of the RSUs over the requisite service period, which is generally the vesting term. For awards only subject to service-based vesting conditions, the Company recognizes stock-based compensation expense on a straight-line basis. For awards subject to performance-based vesting conditions, the Company recognizes stock-based compensation expense using the accelerated attribution method when the achievement of the performance condition becomes probable.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"></p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><b></b></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-05-01_2026-01-31" name="us-gaap:EarningsPerSharePolicyTextBlock" id="c142005104" escape="true"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><b>Net Loss Per Common Share</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:25pt;">Basic net loss per share excludes the effect of dilution and is computed by dividing the net loss attributable to common shareholders by the weighted-average number of shares of Common Stock outstanding during the period, without consideration of potentially dilutive securities.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:25pt;">Diluted net loss per share is computed by dividing the net loss attributable to common shareholders by the weighted-average number of Common Stock and potentially dilutive securities outstanding for the period. For purposes of the diluted net loss per share calculation, convertible preferred stock, stock options, RSUs, Common Stock subject to repurchase related to early exercise of stock options, convertible stock warrants, and convertible notes are considered to be potentially dilutive securities. As the Company has reported a net loss for all periods presented, diluted net loss per common share is the same as basic net loss per common share for those periods.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"></p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b></b></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-05-01_2026-01-31" name="hscs:CommonStockWarrantsPolicyTextBlock" id="c142005105" escape="true"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>Common Stock Warrants</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:25pt;">The Company grants warrants to purchase Common Stock in connection with financing transactions. Warrants are valued based on Black-Scholes models and the fair value is recorded to additional paid-in-capital.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"></p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><b></b></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-05-01_2026-01-31" name="us-gaap:RevenueRecognitionPolicyTextBlock" id="c142005106" escape="true"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><b>Revenue Recognition </b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:25pt;">In accordance with ASC <em style="font: inherit;">606,</em> <i>Revenue from Contracts with Customers,</i> revenue is recognized when a customer obtains control of promised goods or services. The guidance focuses on the core principle for revenue recognition, which is that an entity should recognize revenue to depict the transfer of promised goods or services to customers in an amount that reflects the consideration to which the entity expects to be entitled in exchange for those goods or services. The Company recognizes revenue in accordance with ASC <em style="font: inherit;">606,</em> which provides a <em style="font: inherit;">five</em>-step model for recognizing revenue from contracts with customers as follows:</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;"><tbody><tr><td style="width:25pt;">&#160;</td><td style="vertical-align:top;width:18pt;"> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#9679;</p> </td><td style="vertical-align:top;"> <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Step <em style="font: inherit;">1:</em> Identify the contract(s) with a customer</p> </td></tr>
</tbody></table>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;"><tbody><tr><td style="width:25pt;">&#160;</td><td style="vertical-align:top;width:18pt;"> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#9679;</p> </td><td style="vertical-align:top;"> <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Step <em style="font: inherit;">2:</em> Identify the performance obligations in the contract</p> </td></tr>
</tbody></table>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;"><tbody><tr><td style="width:25pt;">&#160;</td><td style="vertical-align:top;width:18pt;"> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#9679;</p> </td><td style="vertical-align:top;"> <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Step <em style="font: inherit;">3:</em> Determine the transaction price</p> </td></tr>
</tbody></table>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;"><tbody><tr><td style="width:25pt;">&#160;</td><td style="vertical-align:top;width:18pt;"> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#9679;</p> </td><td style="vertical-align:top;"> <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Step <em style="font: inherit;">4:</em> Allocate the transaction price to the performance obligations in the contract</p> </td></tr>
</tbody></table>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;"><tbody><tr><td style="width:25pt;">&#160;</td><td style="vertical-align:top;width:18pt;"> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#9679;</p> </td><td style="vertical-align:top;"> <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Step <em style="font: inherit;">5:</em> Recognize revenue when (or as) the entity satisfies a performance obligation</p> </td></tr>
</tbody></table>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:25pt;">A contract with a customer exists when (i) the Company enters into a legally enforceable contract with a customer, through a purchase order, that defines each party&#8217;s rights regarding the products to be transferred and identifies the payment terms related to these products, (ii) the contract has commercial substance and, (iii) the Company determines that collection of substantially all consideration for products that are transferred is probable based on the customer&#8217;s intent and ability to pay the promised consideration. The only performance obligation is to create and ship the product and each product has separate, distinct pricing. Performance obligations are met and revenue is recognized at a point in time when the order for its goods are shipped FOB manufacturer and control is transferred.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:25pt;">The transaction price is determined based on the amount expected to be entitled to in exchange for transferring the product to the customer net of any transaction price adjustments. The Company&#8217;s payment terms to customers generally range from <em style="font: inherit;">30</em> to <em style="font: inherit;">60</em> days.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:25pt;">Payment terms fall within the <em style="font: inherit;">one</em>-year guidance for the practical expedient which allows the Company to forgo adjustment of the promised amount of consideration for the effects of a significant financing component. The Company accepts product returns at its discretion or if the product is defective as manufactured. Historically, the actual product returns have been immaterial to the Company&#8217;s financial statements. The Company elected to treat shipping and handling costs as a fulfillment cost and included them in the cost of goods sold as incurred. Costs associated with product sales include commissions. The Company applies the practical expedient and recognizes commissions as expense when incurred because the expense is incurred at a point in time and the amortization period is less than <em style="font: inherit;">one</em> year. Commissions are recorded as selling expense.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:25pt;">The Company did <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> recognize material revenues during the&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">nine</em> month periods ended <em style="font: inherit;"> January 31, 2026 </em>and <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>. The Company&#8217;s revenues do <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> require significant estimates or judgments. The Company is <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> a party to contracts that include multiple performance obligations or material variable consideration. As of <em style="font: inherit;"> January 31, 2026</em> and <em style="font: inherit;"> April 30, 2025</em>, the Company did <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c142002250"><span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c142002284"><span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c142002285"><span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c142002286">not</span></span></span></span> have any contract assets or liabilities from contracts with customers and there were <ix:nonFraction id="c142002251" contextRef="i_2026-01-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:RevenueRemainingPerformanceObligation" scale="0" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" decimals="-3">no</ix:nonFraction> remaining performance obligations that the Company had <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> satisfied.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"></p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b></b></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-05-01_2026-01-31" name="us-gaap:IncomeTaxPolicyTextBlock" id="c142005107" escape="true"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>Income Taxes</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:25pt;">The Company accounts for income taxes under the asset and liability method, which requires recognition of deferred tax assets, subject to valuation allowances, and liabilities for the expected future tax consequences of events that have been included in the financial statements or tax returns. Deferred income taxes reflect the net tax effect of temporary differences between the carrying amounts of assets and liabilities for financial reporting and income tax purposes. Management considers many factors when assessing the likelihood of future realization of deferred tax assets, including recent cumulative experience by taxing jurisdiction, expectations of future taxable income or loss, the carry-forward periods available to the Company for tax reporting purposes, and other relevant factors.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:25pt;">In assessing the realizability of deferred tax assets, management considers whether it is more likely than <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> that some portion or all of the deferred tax assets will <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> be realized. The ultimate realization of deferred tax assets is dependent upon the generation of future taxable income during the periods in which those temporary differences become deductible. A valuation allowance is established if it is more likely than <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> that all or a portion of the net deferred tax assets will <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> be realized. Based upon the projections for future taxable income over the periods in which the deferred tax assets are deductible, management believes it is more likely than <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> that the Company will <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> realize the benefits of these deductible differences, and therefore, a full valuation allowance has been recorded at <em style="font: inherit;"> January 31, 2026</em> and <em style="font: inherit;"> April 30, 2025</em>.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:25pt;">Accruals for uncertain tax positions are provided for in accordance with applicable accounting standards. The Company <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>recognize the tax benefits from an uncertain tax position only if it is more likely than <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> that the tax position will be sustained on examination by the taxing authorities, based on the technical merits of the position. The tax benefits recognized in the financial statements from such a position are measured based on the largest benefit that has a greater than <em style="font: inherit;">50%</em> likelihood of being realized upon ultimate settlement. Judgment is required in assessing the future tax consequences of events that have been recognized in the financial statements or tax returns.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:25pt;">Based on its analysis, management has determined that it has <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> incurred any liability for unrecognized tax benefits as of <em style="font: inherit;"> January 31, 2026</em> and <em style="font: inherit;"> April 30, 2025</em>.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:25pt;">The Company <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>be subject to potential examination by U.S. federal, U.S. states or foreign jurisdiction authorities in the areas of income taxes. These potential examinations <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>include questioning the timing and amount of deductions, the nexus of income among various tax jurisdictions and compliance with U.S. federal, U.S. state and foreign tax laws.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:25pt;">The Company is subject to income taxes in the U.S. federal jurisdiction and franchise taxes in the State of Texas. Tax regulations within each jurisdiction are subject to the interpretation of the related tax laws and regulations and require significant judgment to apply. Generally, the Company is <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> longer subject to income tax examinations by major taxing authorities for years before <em style="font: inherit;"> April 30, 2021.</em></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"></p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b></b></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-05-01_2026-01-31" name="us-gaap:SegmentReportingPolicyPolicyTextBlock" id="c142005108" escape="true"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>Segments</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:25pt;">Operating segments are identified as components of an enterprise about which discrete financial information is available for evaluation by the chief operating decision-maker (&#8220;CODM&#8221;) in deciding resource allocation and assessing performance. The Company has determined that its CODM is its Chief Executive Officer. The Company's CODM reviews financial information presented for the purpose of making decisions, allocating resources and evaluating performance. The Company has determined it operates in <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c142002264"><span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c142002288">one</span></span> operating and reportable segment.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"></p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><b></b></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-05-01_2026-01-31" name="us-gaap:NewAccountingPronouncementsPolicyPolicyTextBlock" id="c142005109" escape="true"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><b>Recent Accounting Standards </b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:25pt;">In <em style="font: inherit;"> December 2023, </em>the Financial Standards Accounting Board (FASB) issued Accounting Standards Update (ASU) <em style="font: inherit;">2023</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">09</em> "<i>Income Taxes (Topics <em style="font: inherit;">740</em>): Improvements to Income Tax Disclosures</i>" to expand the disclosure requirements for income taxes, specifically related to the rate reconciliation and income taxes paid. ASU <em style="font: inherit;">2023</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">09</em> is effective for the Company&#8217;s annual periods beginning <em style="font: inherit;"> January 1, 2025, </em>with early adoption permitted. The Company does <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> expect that the standard will have a significant impact on its financial statement disclosures.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:25pt;">In <em style="font: inherit;"> November 2024, </em>the FASB issued ASU <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">03</em> (updated ASU <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">01</em> issued in <em style="font: inherit;"> January 2025), "</em><i>Income Statement - Reporting Comprehensive Income - Expense Disaggregation Disclosures (Subtopic <em style="font: inherit;">220</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">40</em>): Disaggregation of Income Statement Expenses</i>", which requires the disaggregation of certain expense captions into specified categories in disclosures within the notes to the financial statements to provide enhanced transparency into the expense captions presented on the face of the income statement. ASU <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">03</em> is effective for annual reporting periods beginning after <em style="font: inherit;"> December 15, 2026, </em>and interim periods beginning after <em style="font: inherit;"> December 15, 2027, </em>with early adoption permitted, and <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>be applied either prospectively or retrospectively to financial statements issued for reporting periods after the effective date of ASU <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">03</em> or retrospectively to any or all prior periods presented in the financial statements. The Company is currently evaluating the impact of adopting ASU <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">03.</em></p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:25pt;"><em style="font: inherit;"></em></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>

The loan is collateralized by substantially all of the Company&#8217;s assets and intellectual property, except for the secured interest on the covered technology as discussed in Note <em style="font: inherit;">7.</em></p>

The loan was amended in <em style="font: inherit;"> November 2021, </em>extending the maturity to <em style="font: inherit;"> September 30, 2022; </em>further amended in <em style="font: inherit;"> May 2022 </em>to extend the maturity to <em style="font: inherit;"> September 30, 2023; </em>amended again in <em style="font: inherit;"> January 2023 </em>to (i) further extend the maturity date of the FRV Note to <em style="font: inherit;"> September 30, 2024, </em>on which date the principal amount and all accrued interest thereon would be due and payable; and (ii) amend the dates on which principal and accrued interest was due under the JQA Note, such that interest accrued would have been due and payable on <em style="font: inherit;"> September 30, 2023, </em>and the principal amount together with all accrued interest after <em style="font: inherit;"> September 30, 2023 </em>would be due and payable on <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2024.</em></p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>Common Stock</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:25pt;">The Company&#8217;s Certificate of Formation, as amended, authorizes <ix:nonFraction id="c142002493" contextRef="i_2026-01-31" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:CommonStockSharesAuthorized" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">500,000,000</ix:nonFraction> shares of Common Stock. As of <em style="font: inherit;"> January 31, 2026</em> and <em style="font: inherit;"> April 30, 2025</em>, the Company had&#160;<ix:nonFraction id="c142002494" contextRef="i_2026-01-31" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:CommonStockSharesIssued" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">3,184,207</ix:nonFraction>&#160;and <ix:nonFraction id="c142002495" contextRef="i_2025-04-30" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:CommonStockSharesIssued" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">1,119,107</ix:nonFraction>&#160;shares of Common Stock issued and&#160;outstanding, respectively.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:25pt;">During the <em style="font: inherit;">nine</em> months ended <em style="font: inherit;"> January 31, 2026</em>, the Company entered into multiple exchange agreements with Streeterville that exchanged $<ix:nonFraction id="c142002498" contextRef="d_2025-05-01_2026-01-31_DebtConversionByUniqueDescriptionAxis-ConversionOfStreetervilleNoteIntoCommonStockMember" unitRef="USD" name="hscs:DebtConversionOriginalDebtPrincipal" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">1,975,000</ix:nonFraction> in aggregate principal and $<ix:nonFraction id="c142002499" contextRef="d_2025-05-01_2026-01-31_DebtConversionByUniqueDescriptionAxis-ConversionOfStreetervilleNoteIntoCommonStockMember" unitRef="USD" name="hscs:DebtConversionOriginalDebtInterest" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">45,000</ix:nonFraction> of accrued interest of its Streeterville Note for <ix:nonFraction id="c142002500" contextRef="d_2025-05-01_2026-01-31_DebtConversionByUniqueDescriptionAxis-ConversionOfStreetervilleNoteIntoCommonStockMember" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:DebtConversionConvertedInstrumentSharesIssued1" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">570,626</ix:nonFraction> shares of the Company's Common Stock. The issuance of the shares was made pursuant to the exemption from the registration requirements afforded by Section <em style="font: inherit;">3</em>(a)(<em style="font: inherit;">9</em>) of the Securities Act.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:25pt;">During the <em style="font: inherit;">nine</em> months ended <em style="font: inherit;"> January 31, 2026</em>, the Company issued <ix:nonFraction id="c142002504" contextRef="d_2025-05-01_2026-01-31_ConversionOfStockByUniqueDescriptionAxis-ConversionOfSeriesDPreferredIntoCommonStockMember" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:ConversionOfStockSharesIssued1" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">1,375,616</ix:nonFraction> shares of Common Stock as a result of conversions of Series D Preferred Stock.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:25pt;">On <em style="font: inherit;"> September 18, 2023, </em>the Company entered into an Equity Distribution Agreement (the &#8220;EDA&#8221;) with Maxim Group LLC as sales agent pursuant to which the Company <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>offer and sell up to $<ix:nonFraction id="c142002505" contextRef="i_2023-09-30_SubsidiarySaleOfStockAxis-AtmOfferingMember" unitRef="USD" name="hscs:SaleOfStockValueAuthorized" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-4">3.25</ix:nonFraction> million shares of Common Stock under the ATM Facility. The shares <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>be issued and sold from time to time through or to the placement agent acting as sales agent or principal pursuant to our shelf registration statement on Form S-<em style="font: inherit;">3</em> (the &#8220;Shelf S-<em style="font: inherit;">3&#8221;</em>), as filed with the SEC on <em style="font: inherit;"> September 18, 2023. </em>The $<ix:nonFraction id="c142002508" contextRef="i_2023-09-30_SubsidiarySaleOfStockAxis-AtmOfferingMember" unitRef="USD" name="hscs:SaleOfStockValueAuthorized" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-4">3.25</ix:nonFraction> million shares comprised of Common Stock that <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>be offered, issued and sold under the at-the-market offering prospectus is included in the $<ix:nonFraction id="c142002509" contextRef="i_2023-09-28_SubsidiarySaleOfStockAxis-AtmOfferingMember" unitRef="USD" name="hscs:CommonStockValueAuthorized" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-7">50.0</ix:nonFraction> million of securities that <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>be offered, issued, and sold by the Company under the base prospectus of the Shelf S-<em style="font: inherit;">3.</em> The Shelf S-<em style="font: inherit;">3</em> was declared effective by the SEC on <em style="font: inherit;"> September 28, 2023.</em></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:25pt;">On <em style="font: inherit;"> November 9, 2023, </em>the Company entered into Amendment <em style="font: inherit;">No.</em> <em style="font: inherit;">1</em> to the EDA with Maxim, pursuant to which the Company <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>sell up to $<ix:nonFraction id="c142002514" contextRef="i_2023-11-09_SubsidiarySaleOfStockAxis-AtmOfferingMember" unitRef="USD" name="hscs:SaleOfStockValueAuthorized" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-7">10.0</ix:nonFraction> million shares of Common Stock from time to time through the sales agent.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:25pt;">On <em style="font: inherit;"> November 17, 2023, </em>the Company entered into Amendment <em style="font: inherit;">No.</em> <em style="font: inherit;">2</em> to the EDA with Maxim, pursuant to which the Company <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>sell up to $<ix:nonFraction id="c142002517" contextRef="i_2023-11-17_SubsidiarySaleOfStockAxis-AtmOfferingMember" unitRef="USD" name="hscs:SaleOfStockValueAuthorized" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-6">15.0</ix:nonFraction> million shares of Common Stock from time to time through the sales agent.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:25pt;">On <em style="font: inherit;"> August 3, 2025, </em>the Company entered into Amendment <em style="font: inherit;">No.</em> <em style="font: inherit;">3</em> to the EDA with Maxim Group pursuant to which the Company <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>offer and sell, from time to time, up to $<ix:nonFraction id="c142002520" contextRef="i_2025-08-03_SubsidiarySaleOfStockAxis-AtmOfferingMember" unitRef="USD" name="hscs:SaleOfStockValueAuthorized" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">25,000,000</ix:nonFraction> of shares of Common Stock and the parties further agreed that Maxim will be entitled to compensation at a commission rate equal to <ix:nonFraction id="c142002521" contextRef="i_2025-08-03_SubsidiarySaleOfStockAxis-AtmOfferingMember" unitRef="Pure" name="hscs:CommissionRate" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="2">4.0</ix:nonFraction>% of the gross sales price per share sold pursuant to the EDA up to a maximum of $<ix:nonFraction id="c142002522" contextRef="d_2025-08-03_2025-08-03_RangeAxis-MaximumMember_SubsidiarySaleOfStockAxis-AtmOfferingMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:ProceedsFromIssuanceOfCommonStock" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">11,036,310</ix:nonFraction> in gross proceeds to the Company, and <ix:nonFraction id="c142002523" contextRef="i_2025-08-03_SubsidiarySaleOfStockAxis-AtmOfferingMember" unitRef="Pure" name="hscs:PercentOfGrossSalesPrice" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="2">3.0</ix:nonFraction>% of the gross sales price per share sold pursuant to the EDA from any gross proceeds to the Company in excess of such amount; provided, however, that in <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> event will the Company issue or sell through the Sales Agent such number of shares of Common Stock that would cause the Company or the offering of its shares of Common Stock to <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> satisfy the eligibility and transaction requirements for use of Form S-<em style="font: inherit;">3</em> (including General Instruction <em style="font: inherit;">I.B.6</em> of Form S-<em style="font: inherit;">3</em>).&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:25pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:25pt;">During the <em style="font: inherit;">nine</em> months ended <em style="font: inherit;"> January 31, 2026</em>, the Company issued and sold <ix:nonFraction id="c142002530" contextRef="d_2025-05-01_2026-01-31_SubsidiarySaleOfStockAxis-AtmOfferingMember" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:StockIssuedDuringPeriodSharesNewIssues" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">48,858</ix:nonFraction> shares of Common Stock under the ATM Facility.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:25pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:25pt;">During the&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">nine</em> months ended <em style="font: inherit;"> January 31, 2026</em>, the Company issued <ix:nonFraction id="c142002532" contextRef="d_2025-05-01_2026-01-31_AwardTypeAxis-RestrictedStockMember" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:StockIssuedDuringPeriodSharesNewIssues" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">70,000</ix:nonFraction> shares of restricted stock to management. See further discussion in Note <em style="font: inherit;">6.</em>&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:25pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:25pt;">The holders of Common Stock are entitled to receive dividends whenever funds and assets are legally available and when declared by the board of directors, subject to the rights of holders of Preferred Stock outstanding. <ix:nonFraction id="c142002534" contextRef="d_2025-05-01_2026-01-31" unitRef="USDPerShare" name="us-gaap:CommonStockDividendsPerShareDeclared" scale="0" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" decimals="-3">No</ix:nonFraction> dividends were declared as of or through the <em style="font: inherit;">nine</em> months ended <em style="font: inherit;"> January 31, 2026</em> and the year ended <em style="font: inherit;"> April 30, 2025</em>.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
